newsitem.title: USA: Lucent, Philips form $2.5 billion phone company.
newsitem.headline: Lucent, Philips form $2.5 billion phone company.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc. and Philips Electronics NV of the Netherlands said Tuesday they will combine their consumer telephone and related businesses in a jointly owned company with annual sales of about $2.5 billion.

The company, to be called Philips Consumer Communications, combines two of the largest makers of phones, cordless phones, and other equipment in the United States and Europe. The venture, to be 60 percent-owned by Philips with the rest owned by Lucent, will need to play catch-up in the market for cellular phones, pagers and other products, analysts said.
No cash will change hands in the transaction.

The venture brings together the $1.4 billion consumer products business of Philips, Europe's biggest electronics company, and the $1.1 billion consumer telephone business at Lucent, the former equipment-making arm of AT&T Corp. that was spun off last year. It will have more than 12,000 employees and few cuts are expected.

Analysts and company officials said the combination was an excellent fit and would strengthen Philips' presence in the United States and free Lucent to focus on its more profitable telephone network equipment business.
"Three of Lucent's four main businesses are absolute home runs," SBC Warburg analyst Barry Sine said of Lucent's network systems, business communications and semiconductor operations.
"One of them -- consumer products -- is more of a question mark," Sine said. "This deal puts Lucent's consumer products business on more of a strategic footing."

"The partnership we are forming with Philips is a near-perfect fit for both companies," said Carly Fiorina, who heads Lucent's existing consumer products business and will serve as a board member of the new venture. "What each company needed was exactly what the other company had."
Philips is the leading maker of corded and cordless phones in Europe, and Lucent is the biggest maker of phones and answering machines in the United States.

The venture will be the fourth largest in consumer phone equpiment behind Motorola Inc., Finland's Nokia AB Oy and Sweden's Ericsson, with greatest strength in the slowest growing part of the market -- phones, cordless phones and answering machines.
Lucent's consumer products business has been a drag on other parts of the company, such as network equipment, which are growing at more than 20 percent a year, Sine said.
Still, the Lucent business operates at a modest profit, company officials said in a telephone conference call.
"This joint venture will be profitable from day one," said Michael McTighe, managing director of Philips' existing consumer electronics business, who will be chief executive of the new venture.

Both parent companies plan to supply additional funding to develop the joint venture. They will also continue to provide the venture access to other operations, such as Lucent's research and development operations.
The venture will be based in Parsippany, N.J., near Lucent's Murray Hill, N.J., headquarters, while a search for a permanent base takes place, officials said.
The executives said the new venture took shape quickly after talks began two to three months ago, which officials credited to the lack of overlap in the companies' operations.
The companies said they expect "the vast majority" of the 8,400 Lucent and the 4,000 Philips employees in their consumer telephone businesses to move to the new venture.
Lucent stock rose $2.125 to $69.75 and Philips U.S. shares jumped $3 to $66.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
